A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 32-page BlurDM paper, including Appendices A.1–A.10. Text extraction and rendering support a complete comparison: pages 2–32 are textually and visually identical; page 1 differs only in the resource-link sentence and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original deblurring experiments, quantitative comparisons, and ablations in Section 4, with additional training-cost, diffusion-step, and qualitative results in Appendices A.5–A.9.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses, including numerical results in Tables 1–8 and qualitative deblurring results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dual noise/blur diffusion, reverse process, latent prior generator, encoders, fusion module, losses, and three-stage training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use GoPro, HIDE, RealBlur-J, and RealBlur-R for the same deblurring tasks. Appendix exposure-based visualizations and real-world evaluation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MIMO-UNet, Stripformer, FFTformer, and LoFormer baselines. Table 3 retains MLP, DDPM, and RDDM prior comparisons; Table 5 retains HI-Diff and RDDM. Appendix comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, training budgets, default five-step diffusion setting, and testing procedures are identical in Section 4 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Estimator and training-stage ablations, iteration sensitivity, computational and training-cost analyses, and blur-residual visualizations are unchanged in Section 4.3 and Appendices A.5–A.8.

E5.justification: Both retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices. Checklist item 7 explicitly states that error bars and statistical significance tests are omitted because of computational expense.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and all qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains GoPro PSNR values of 32.44 dB for baseline MIMO-UNet and 32.93 dB with BlurDM.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A.1–A.4 retain identical equations and derivations for forward diffusion, the ELBO and optimization, deterministic sampling, and the latent-space justification.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about incorporating blur formation into diffusion and improving four deblurring models across four benchmarks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of blur-residual modeling, complementary estimators, and training-stage benefits are unchanged. Section 5 retains the defocus-blur limitation, and the appendix retains the same mechanism and broader-impact discussions.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a direct GitHub source-code link with a GitHub Pages project-page link. This changes the stated access route; implementation details and the checklist's code-availability statement remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish any actual change in code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2, comparisons with prior diffusion approaches, and the bibliography are identical. No cited work or substantive research-positioning statement changes.

P1.justification: The abstract's final sentence changes from announcing source code to announcing a project page, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other wording and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and eight tables retain their designs, captions, contents, and placement. Page layout is unchanged, and pages 2–32 have pixel-identical renderings.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, limitations, and organization are identical. The resource-link substitution and updated arXiv stamp do not establish a meaningful quality improvement or decline; the PDFs show no material reproducibility gain or loss.
